citation.authors: Hadi A, Pourmasoumi M, Najafgholizadeh A, Clark CCT et al

cited_by.title: Apple cider vinegar: weight, blood sugar and safety

record.population: Adults in nine randomised trials (ten study arms) of apple cider vinegar for at least two weeks (ethnicity not stated in the abstract)
record.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials: lipids and blood sugar
record.finding: Apple cider vinegar lowered total cholesterol by about 6 mg/dL, fasting glucose by about 8 mg/dL and HbA1c by 0.5 points. There was no effect on LDL, HDL, insulin or HOMA-IR. Results were stronger in people with type 2 diabetes and with longer use, and variation between studies was moderate to high.
